name: Claudius
overview: Claudius Lysias was a male Roman military officer who served as the commander of the Roman garrison in Jerusalem. His role placed him in a position of authority within the Roman administrative and military structure in the city. Beyond his military leadership, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The individual is referred to as Claudius Lysias and also simply as Lysias in Scripture. There are no specific Hebrew or Greek meanings provided for these names, so they are presented plainly as proper names used in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Claudius Lysias beyond what is noted in his official capacity as commander of the Roman garrison. No further personal or familial connections are detailed.
scriptureSignificance: Claudius Lysias is significant in the biblical narrative as the Roman authority overseeing Jerusalem's garrison, which situates him at a critical intersection between Roman governance and the early Christian movement. His leadership role implies involvement in maintaining order during the events recorded in Acts. This highlights the Roman context in which the early church operated and the challenges faced by believers under imperial rule.
